name: TX-20
label: Safe D

Castro's incumbency and 10-to-1 fundraising advantage over Baez

model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean, Castro's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising edge make an upset implausible, and prediction markets agree at roughly 98% for Castro. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals-based margin of about 23 points stands.
model.watch: A major red-wave polling shift in Texas urban districts or an unexpected Castro scandal would be the main things to watch, though neither appears likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in this San Antonio-area House district, which leans Democratic by about 16 points. He is a well-established incumbent who has consistently won comfortably, and he has raised over $500,000 for the race. His Republican opponent, Edgardo Rafael Baez, has raised under $50,000 and has no visible outside support.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and markets. Polymarket prices Castro's chances at about 98%. The expected margin is roughly 23 points, with Castro a heavy favorite.
